extracted.intended_audience: Public housing authorities (PHAs), PBRA owners/manager/landlords, tenant advocates, legal service providers, and HUD policymakers
extracted.subtask_description: Extracts the substantive criteria and comment-response standards for HUD's rule establishing a 30-day notice requirement for nonpayment-based lease terminations in specified HUD programs, including required notice content, accessibility, repayment agreements, state-law interaction, implementation timelines, and scope issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Itemized rent breakdown and cure date in 30-day notice
rubrics_metrics.description: Require an itemized breakdown by month of the alleged rent owed by the tenant, along with any other arrearages allowed by HUD and included in the lease, and the date by which the tenant must pay the amount of rent owed before a formal judicial eviction can be filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commenters requested this detail so tenants can clearly see what is owed and the exact cure deadline. HUD's rule requires that the 30-day notice include instructions on how tenants can cure lease violations for nonpayment of rent.

rubrics_metrics.name: VAWA notice of rights and self-certification
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure provision of Violence Against Women Act (VAWA) notices and self-certification forms at required junctures (when tenants are admitted to programs, when there is an eviction and/or termination notice, and when there's a denial of assistance).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some commenters urged that the rule require inclusion of VAWA information in the 30-day notice; HUD states this rule does not change existing VAWA notification requirements and notes some providers include the notice at other junctures (e.g., recertifications).

rubrics_metrics.name: Instructions on how to cure nonpayment (how to avoid termination)
rubrics_metrics.description: 30-day notice must include instructions on how tenants can cure lease violations for nonpayment of rent (in practice, paying the back rent owed).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These instructions should allow tenants to take steps to avoid lease termination and potential eviction; HUD emphasizes focusing on notification requirements, with tenants generally curing nonpayment by paying back rent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interim recertification and minimum-rent hardship exemption information
rubrics_metrics.description: Include information on how tenants can recertify their income (interim recertification) if applicable, and how tenants can request a minimum rent hardship exemption if applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commenters urged HUD to require plain-language templates informing tenants of interim recertification and hardship exemption rights, to state what may qualify a family for hardship, and to report use/outcomes of hardship exemptions; HUD requires the 30-day notice to include recertification/hardship-exemption instructions and will determine additional guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Local legal and rental assistance resources (proposed)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide local nonprofit resources, agencies, organizations, and information on right-to-counsel laws, fair housing rights, and tenant rights in the notice so tenants can get assistance finding housing, financial help, and legal representation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commenters argued this is impactful and not an undue burden; HUD declined to require notices to contain non-Federal resource lists (impractical to be exhaustive) but encourages PHAs/owners to share knowledge of available rental assistance resources and sample language for PHA plans.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accessibility and language access of notices
rubrics_metrics.description: Notices, lease amendments, and notifications of lease changes must be provided in plain language and in accessible formats for individuals with disabilities and in translated formats to provide meaningful access for people with limited English proficiency (LEP).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Suggested formats include screen-reader-friendly electronic versions, Braille, and backup oral interpretation. PHAs/owners must comply with section 504, title II of the ADA, and title VI obligations; give primary consideration to the auxiliary aids/services preferred by the individual and take reasonable steps for LEP meaningful access.

rubrics_metrics.name: Repayment agreements — require vs. encourage and model plan features
rubrics_metrics.description: Commenters urged HUD to require (rather than recommend) PHAs and PBRA owners to enter into reasonable rental repayment agreements and to prohibit requiring lump-sum payments alone.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Suggested model repayment plan features: affordability such that monthly repayment plus current rent does not exceed 40% of household adjusted income; include amount owed (excluding fines/fees), date back rent was calculated, monthly payment amount broken down between back rent and current rent, repayment period, and a rent ledger; must be renegotiated if adjusted income decreases by 10% or more; must not require lump sums; suspend agreement without additional arrearages (late fees, attorney/admin fees) if household demonstrates insufficient income; establish quarterly check-ins during suspension; ensure plan materials comply with Federal civil rights law to provide meaningful access for LEP persons. HUD's response: will not require repayment plans in this rule but strongly encourages them and plans to issue updated repayment guidance incorporating civil rights obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preemption/interplay with state law and prohibition on filing eviction before 30 days
rubrics_metrics.description: Clarify that tenants have the right to cure a nonpayment lease violation within 30 days of the termination notice and that this right preempts any state law that provides less protection to tenants; prohibit landlords from using state eviction procedures to subvert federal notice protections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commenters pointed to state laws (e.g., Florida) that can require payment into court registries or allow filings despite defective notices. HUD revised the rule to specify a PHA/owner must not provide a termination notice before the day after rent is due and must not proceed with filing an eviction if the tenant pays the alleged amount owed within the 30-day notification period; HUD states the final rule applies irrespective of state/local law and prohibits filing before the 30-day notice expires.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope limitation to nonpayment-based evictions (other causes outside rule)
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the 30-day notice applies to lease violations beyond nonpayment (e.g., material noncompliance, failure to recertify, cleanliness, unauthorized occupants, pets, smoking) was raised by commenters who urged expansion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: HUD's response: comments beyond evictions for nonpayment are outside the scope of this rulemaking, though HUD may consider such suggestions in the future.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice period length (30 days vs. longer periods)
rubrics_metrics.description: Debate over whether the notice period should be longer (45–90 days) to give tenants more time to seek assistance, navigate recertifications, adjust paperwork, secure legal counsel, or find housing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commenters argued for 60–90 days citing time needed for documentation, administrative processing, and needs of seniors/people with disabilities; HUD concluded 30 days best balances tenants' interests and PHAs/owners' ability to operate effectively and retains the 30-day period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emergency declarations and inclusion of emergency rental assistance information
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the rule should trigger expanded tenant protections or require notice content specific to presidentially declared national emergencies or Stafford Act disasters and include information on available federal/state/local emergency rental assistance programs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commenters requested application during presidential or gubernatorial disaster declarations and inclusion of local/state/charitable rental assistance information. HUD's response: the rule provides protections irrespective of national emergency and gives the Secretary flexibility to require information tailored to a national emergency, but HUD will not require specific information for presidentially declared emergencies at this time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Implementation timeline for lease amendments and effective compliance dates
rubrics_metrics.description: Timing for when PHAs and PBRA owners must incorporate the 30-day notice requirement into leases and when the rule's notice requirements become binding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commenters urged immediate effect or shorter compliance windows; HUD determined: allow PHAs 18 months from the effective date to comply with lease provision/addendum incorporation, and PBRA owners 14 months from HUD publication of a final model lease (HUD plans to issue model leases within a year of the rule's effective date). HUD will issue a Federal Register document to advise when model leases are available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance oversight, reporting, and required delivery methods (proposals)
rubrics_metrics.description: Mechanisms for HUD oversight and enforcement of the rule, including reporting of nonpayment eviction initiations with demographic data (race, ethnicity, age, income), random file pulls to assess compliance, tenant reporting mechanisms for noncompliance, and specification of delivery methods for the 30-day notice (e.g., certified mail with receipt, hand delivery to a household member above age 16 with tenant acknowledgement).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commenters urged HUD to clarify oversight, enforcement actions, update systems, amend model leases and HUD handbooks (e.g., 4350.3), and specify delivery methods to ensure notice is received; HUD acknowledged implementation time and civil rights protections apply and plans guidance/model language.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion of additional HUD programs for uniformity (HCV, PBV, RAD, LIHTC-associated assistance)
rubrics_metrics.description: Commenters urged that the 30-day notice requirement be extended to other HUD-governed subsidy types (Housing Choice Vouchers (HCV), Project-Based Vouchers (PBV), Rental Assistance Demonstration (RAD) conversions, LIHTC properties with federal assistance) to create a uniform standard and avoid confusion and disparate protections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Arguments include operational simplicity for landlords/managers, protection parity for tenants across subsidy types, and preventing lower standards for voucher holders. Commenters cited HUD's authority to include such programs; HUD response in this chunk does not finalize expansion but recognizes the comments and the rationale.
